Yet
YET
conj. / adv.
Webster 1828 treats YET first as a conjunction: nevertheless; notwithstanding; however. He then lists the adverbial uses: beside; still; at this time / so soon (Not yet); at least; a little longer; still, in a new degree; even, after all; hitherto. His own biblical illustration is Matthew 6:29 (YET I say unto you…). This page fills the KJV-gap particle. Companion pages already treat nevertheless, sinner, and hope.

Biblical Definition

Yet in Scripture is not a stall and not a loophole. It names what has not come, what remains true against appearance, and what was true of us when Christ died. Jesus will not let His mother hurry the hour: mine hour is not yet come (John 2:4). Paul will not let the cross wait for our improvement: while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us (Rom 5:8). He will not let the servant of Christ keep a second master: if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ (Gal 1:10). Habakkuk will not let empty barns cancel worship: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation (Hab 3:18). John will not let present sonship pretend to be finished glory: it doth not yet appear what we shall be (1 John 3:2). The dictionary therefore keeps yet from becoming either delay-of-obedience or denial-of-hope. It is the Bible’s way of saying: still, nevertheless, and not yet — on God’s clock, not ours.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines YET as a conjunction (nevertheless; notwithstanding; however) and as an adverb: beside; still; at this time / not yet; at least; a little longer; still in a new degree; even after all; hitherto.

expand to see more

YET, conjunction [Gr.] Nevertheless; notwithstanding; however. I come to you in the spirit of peace; yet you will not receive me.

YET I say unto you, the Solomon in all his glory, was not arrayed like one of these. Matthew 6:29.

YET, adverb

1. Beside; over and above. There is one reason yet further to be alledged.

2. Still; the state remaining the same.

They attest facts they had heard while they were yet heathens.

3. At this time; so soon. Is it time to go? Not yet.

4. At least; at all.

5. It is prefixed to words denoting extension of time or continuance. A little longer; yet a little longer.

6. Still; in a new degree. The crime becomes yet blacker by the pretense of piety.

7. Even; after all; a kind of emphatical addition to a negative.

8. Hitherto. You have yet done nothing; you have as yet done less than was expected.

Key Scripture

John 2:4 — "Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come."

Romans 5:8 — "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."

Galatians 1:10 — "For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ."

Habakkuk 3:18 — "Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation."

1 John 3:2 — "Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is."

Modern Corruption

Yet is corrupted when not yet is used to postpone obedience, when yet sinners is used to postpone repentance, and when men-pleasing is kept as a second service beside Christ.

expand to see more

The first corruption is to steal John 2:4. Mine hour is not yet come is the Son’s clock, not a license to delay what He has already commanded. Soft religion treats every hard duty as not yet. The recovery is: where Scripture has spoken, the hour has come.

The second corruption is cheap grace wearing Romans 5:8. While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us is particular love at the cross, not permission to remain in the sin. Antinomian talk hears yet as forever. Paul hears it as the time of our death in Adam, already met by Christ’s death for the elect.

The third corruption is Galatians 1:10 with a smile. If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ is not a branding problem. Attractional ministry and people-pleasing pulpits keep a second yet. The servant of Christ cannot keep it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: nevertheless / still / not yet. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek oupo (G3768) at John 2:4 and 1 John 3:2 (not yet); Greek eti (G2089) at Romans 5:8 and Galatians 1:10. Habakkuk 3:18 carries no Strong’s tag on Yet in this cache; this page does not mint a Hebrew number for that line.

expand to see more

Greek oupo (G3768) — not yet (John 2:4; 1 John 3:2).

Greek eti (G2089) — yet, still, even now (Rom 5:8, yet sinners; Gal 1:10, if I yet pleased men).

Habakkuk 3:18 is KJV-verified; the cache does not tag Yet with a Hebrew number on that verse line. No lemma is invented here.

Matthew 6:29 English And yet sits on G1161 (de) in this cache; that connective is not treated as a minted yet-lemma on this page.

Usage

"Mine hour is not yet come (John 2:4) — the Son’s clock, not a delay of commanded duty."

"Christ died for us while we were yet sinners (Rom 5:8); that yet is the time of our ruin, not a forever permit."

"Habakkuk will yet rejoice when the fields fail (Hab 3:18); Paul will not yet please men and still be Christ’s servant (Gal 1:10)."
